learning_objective: 🎯 Understand George Bernard Shaw's witty and provocative argument that true individual freedom is an illusion in modern society, where we are all enslaved by our biological needs and economic systems!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Shaw divides our bondage into two types: 'Natural slavery' is our biological need to eat, sleep, and clothe ourselves to survive. 'Unnatural slavery' is the social and economic compulsion where one man is forced to work for another man's profit.

According to Shaw, a truly free person is someone who can do whatever they like with their own time without any external compulsion. However, because of biological and societal demands, total freedom is impossible.

main_concepts.concept_title: 💰 The Illusion of Freedom for the Poor
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Shaw argues that wage-workers are merely 'wage-slaves.' They believe they are free because they can vote or change employers, but they are still forced to spend their lives working just to earn basic survival.
Even the wealthy aren't truly free—they shift their share of natural work onto the working class, becoming socially dependent parasites who are trapped by social customs and anxieties.

fun_activity.title: ⏰ The 24-Hour Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Track your 24 hours today. How many hours went to 'Natural Slavery' (sleeping, eating, chores), how many to 'Unnatural Compulsion' (forced work/study), and how many hours were genuinely 'Free Leisure'?

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define Shaw's distinction between 'Natural Slavery' (imposed by Nature) and 'Unnatural Slavery' (imposed by Man on Man).
📌 Explain why Shaw calls the modern capitalist society an elaborate disguise for slavery.
📌 Use Shaw's famous ironic style: he uses paradoxes and sharp satire to force readers to question their common-sense beliefs about liberty.
quick_recap: ⭐ Shaw was a renowned playwright and a socialist philosopher (Fabian Society member).
⭐ He argues that laws and constitutions can declare a man free, but hunger and poverty make him a slave.
⭐ The essay concludes that society must be reorganized so that daily labor and leisure are shared fairly among all people.
